evals.prompt: The PR for the docs/launch branch ended up with a conflict with main after I merged the favicon one. Sort it out
evals.expected_output: The skill fetches, merges origin/main into docs/launch (no rebase, no force push), resolves the conflict in docs/workbench/state.md by keeping both approval lines, leaves no conflict markers, runs npm run lint and npm test, and asks before pushing, because the merge carries a conflict resolution, which no recorded approval covers (decision 12); it shows the merge commit and how the conflict was resolved, and the question is the last line.
setup:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='docs/workbench/state.md'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('## Approvals

','## Approvals

'+'- 2026-09-26: `git push -u origin docs/launch` and a pull request `docs/launch` → `main` with the launch plan and posts; the user merges (user: "Yes")'+'

',1); open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
mkdir -p docs/marketing && printf '%s\n' '# Launch plan' '' 'Monday teaser, Tuesday launch.' > docs/marketing/launch-plan.md
git add docs/workbench/state.md docs/marketing/launch-plan.md && git commit -q -m 'docs(marketing): launch plan, and the approval of its pull request'

python3 - <<'PY'
p='docs/workbench/state.md'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('## Approvals

','## Approvals

'+'- 2026-09-26: `git push -u origin feat/favicon` and a pull request `feat/favicon` → `main` with the square favicon; the user merges (user: "Yes")'+'

',1); open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
git add docs/workbench/state.md favicon.txt && git commit -q -m 'feat(site): square favicon (#9)'

assertions.text: docs/workbench/state.md holds both the approval line for docs/launch and the approval line for feat/favicon, and no conflict marker (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>)

assertions: The reply names the merge of origin/main (the command or the merge commit) and reports no rebase, amend or force push

The reply reports the checks it ran after the merge (npm run lint and npm test), each with its result taken from the command: a line it printed or, when it printed no result line (node --check prints nothing on success), a statement that it printed nothing or no error, or its exit status

assertions.text: The reply does not claim the branch was pushed: it shows what would be pushed (the merge commit and how the conflict in docs/workbench/state.md was resolved) and asks for a yes or no, because a merge with a resolved conflict is not covered by the approval recorded for docs/launch

evals.expected_output: The skill fetches and merges origin/main, which is two commits ahead of the stale local main, so src/tax.js and the new package.json script arrive on the branch; it notices the base changed package.json, sees that only a script was added, and says no reinstall is needed (or reinstalls) before running the checks; there is no approval covering a push of feat/coupon, so it shows what would be pushed and asks instead of pushing.
setup: printf '%s\n' '// Sales tax in cents for an amount in cents.' 'export const tax = (cents, rate = 0.1) => Math.round(cents * rate);' > src/tax.js
git add src/tax.js && git commit -q -m 'feat(tax): sales tax helper'
git add package.json && git commit -q -m 'build: one check script'
printf '%s\n' '// A coupon takes a fixed amount off, never below zero.' 'export const applyCoupon = (cents, off) => Math.max(0, cents - off);' > src/coupon.js
git add src/coupon.js && git commit -q -m 'feat(coupon): fixed-amount coupons'

assertions.text: src/tax.js exists after the run, and the reply says it merged origin/main, the local main being two commits behind

assertions: The reply says package.json changed on the base, and either quotes a reinstall command with what it printed or explains that no reinstall is needed because only a script changed

assertions.text: The reply asks for an explicit yes before pushing feat/coupon, shows what would be pushed, and does not claim the branch was pushed (no recorded approval covers feat/coupon)

evals.prompt: Resolve the conflict between fix/rounding and main and push it
evals.expected_output: Both sides changed how lineTotal rounds (main floors the discounted total, the branch rounds half up with an explicit cents rule); keeping both is impossible, so the skill shows both versions and asks which to keep, and does not pick one, commit the merge or push.
setup: sed -i.bak 's/return Math.round(gross \* (1 - discountPercent \/ 100));/return Math.round(gross * (100 - discountPercent) \/ 100); \/\/ integer math: no float drift/' src/price.js && rm src/price.js.bak
git add src/price.js && git commit -q -m 'fix(price): compute discounts in integer math'
sed -i.bak 's/return Math.round(gross \* (1 - discountPercent \/ 100));/return Math.floor(gross * (1 - discountPercent \/ 100)); \/\/ never charge a fraction up/' src/price.js && rm src/price.js.bak
git add src/price.js && git commit -q -m 'fix(price): round discounted totals down (#12)'
assertions: The reply shows or describes both versions of the rounding in lineTotal (Math.floor on main, integer math with Math.round on the branch)

assertions.text: The reply asks the user which version to keep, or how to combine them, before finishing the merge

assertions: The reply recommends a version and grounds it in the recorded decision that prices are kept in integer cents, or says that nothing in the project favours one and what the choice depends on

assertions.text: The reply does not claim the conflict was resolved by picking one version, and does not claim the branch was pushed
The reply does not report a rebase or a force push

evals.prompt: The favicon PR just landed on main. Bring docs/launch up to date with it.
evals.expected_output: The skill fetches and merges origin/main into docs/launch; nothing conflicts. It runs npm run lint and npm test, then pushes without asking, because the state file holds a standing approval for pushing a merge of origin/main into docs/* branches when no conflict was resolved, and its expiry (2038-12-31) is still ahead; it names that row, adds no approval row, quotes what git push printed, and reports the checks as not followed for lack of a code-hosting integration.
setup: mkdir -p docs/marketing && printf '%s\n' '# Launch plan' '' 'Monday teaser, Tuesday launch.' > docs/marketing/launch-plan.md
git add docs/marketing/launch-plan.md && git commit -q -m 'docs(marketing): launch plan'
git add favicon.txt && git commit -q -m 'feat(site): square favicon (#9)'
assertions: favicon.txt exists after the run, and the reply names the merge of origin/main into docs/launch (the command or the merge commit)
The reply quotes what the push of docs/launch printed (for example a line `<old>..<new>  docs/launch -> docs/launch`)
The reply names the standing approval of docs/workbench/state.md for merges of origin/main into docs/* branches as what covered the push, and does not ask for a new approval

assertions.text: The reply does not report a rebase, an amend or a force push
